patch_description: Replace the single-trajectory simulated annealing (which regressed to 2.38 from the 2.40 greedy hill-climb) with a multi-start greedy hill-climb: each of 4 starts begins from the best lattice candidate perturbed with a distinct ±0.01 Gaussian jitter, and the time budget is split evenly with shrinking per-start deadlines ((deadline−now)/(n_starts−start)). The hill-climb itself keeps the LP re-solve and adaptive step-size shrink/grow schedule that previously broke 2.40. Jittered variants of a strong base have empirically beaten diverse layouts, and decorrelating the starts cheaply samples more basins within the same wall-clock time. Also expand the seed candidate list slightly so the base itself is stronger before jittering.
